mainTopic: Mourning on שבת and festivals: which mourning signs stop, the rules of קריעה, private mourning practices, and the ban on relations during אבילות.
overview: The amud opens with שמואל's answer to רבי יוחנן: there is no אבילות on שבת. Next, רב פפא corrects a report. Relations during אבילות are only אסור, and that ruling came from רבי יוחנן. The 'חייב מיתה' ruling of שמואל is really about an אבל who skips פריעה and פרימה, and it is learned from a פסוק in ויקרא. A ברייתא in אבל רבתי backs up the איסור. שמואל then lists which mourning signs must be dropped on שבת (פח״ז) and which are optional (נת״ר), and רב argues about uncovering the head. The גמרא explains שמואל's view through his unusual ישמעאלים-style head-wrap. It then tests his rule that tearing counts only בשעת חימום, and finds exceptions for a sage and for a parent. Next comes a מחלוקת about mending the extra tears for a parent. Then the principle that private mourning practices continue on שבת. The amud ends with שמואל's ruling like רבן גמליאל on holidays, and another version that places that ruling on a ברייתא about burying a baby.

steps.title: Is there mourning on שבת?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks שמואל whether the laws of אבילות apply on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן asked שמואל: Is there mourning on שבת, or is there no mourning on שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן asks שמואל a yes-or-no question about whether an אבל keeps his mourning practices on שבת. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question has two sides: either אבילות continues on שבת like any other day, or שבת pushes it away completely. He is asking about mourning on שבת in general, not about one specific practice.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked of him (a formal question to a scholar)
Mourning, the set of practices an אבל keeps

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan asked of Shmuel:
Is there mourning on Shabbat
or is there no mourning on Shabbat?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשְּׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic within the laws of אבילות.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the practices of אבילות are kept on שבת.

steps.title: There is no mourning on שבת
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that there is no אבילות on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There is no mourning on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives his answer: the mourning practices do not apply on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is short and absolute: 'אין אבילות בשבת.' On שבת the אבל does not keep his mourning, even though the mourning days still continue around it.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל rules: אין אבילות בשבת. There is no mourning on שבת.

phrases.english: He said to him: There is no mourning on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֵין אֲבֵילוּת בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is no אבילות on שבת.

steps.title: A report in שמואל's name: a mourner who had relations deserves death
steps.stepSummary: Some רבנן sitting before רב פפא quote שמואל as saying that an אבל who had relations during his mourning days is liable to מיתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages sat before רב פפא and said in the name of שמואל: A mourner who had marital relations during his days of mourning is liable to death.
steps.whatsHappening: A group of scholars repeats a very harsh ruling in שמואל's name about an אבל and תשמיש המטה. This sets up רב פפא's correction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim is that breaking this rule is not just forbidden but is punishable by death. Watch carefully: both the strength of the rule and the name it is quoted in are about to be challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages were sitting before him

phrases.english: The Sages were sitting before Rav Pappa
and saying in the name of Shmuel:
A mourner who had relations during his days of mourning
is liable to death.
phrases.notes: This means death at the hands of שמים, not a court punishment.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתְבִי רַבָּנַן קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא וְקָאָמְרִי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new statement about אבילות, separate from the שבת question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: As reported: an אבל who had relations during אבילות is liable to מיתה.

steps.title: רב פפא corrects the report: only forbidden, and said by רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the real ruling was only 'אסור', and it was said in רבי יוחנן's name, not שמואל's.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to them: It was said 'forbidden,' and it was said in the name of רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא rejects the report from step 3 and fixes it on two points.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, the punishment was overstated: the original ruling only said the act is forbidden, with no death penalty. Second, the speaker was wrong: the ruling came from רבי יוחנן, not שמואל.
steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא agrees that relations during אבילות are forbidden. He only denies the death penalty and the name it was quoted in.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to them:
"Forbidden" is what was said,
and it was said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא: אָסוּר אִתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corrects the report of step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Both the severity (death) and the attribution (שמואל) of the report.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The rabbis mixed up two statements. The ruling on relations was only 'אסור' and came from רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: What שמואל really said: a mourner who did not let his hair grow and tear his clothes
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the 'liable to death' statement in שמואל's name was about an אבל who did not do פריעה and פרימה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you heard something in שמואל's name, this is what you heard: רב תחליפא בר אבימי said that שמואל said: A mourner who did not let his hair grow wild and did not tear his clothes is liable to death.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא continues and shows where the 'חייב מיתה' they remembered actually came from. It was a different statement of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's death-penalty ruling is about failing to do the mourning practices of פריעה (letting the hair grow) and פרימה (tearing the clothes). It has nothing to do with תשמיש המטה. So the רבנן had attached the wrong subject to שמואל's words.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the mistake: two different 'אבל' rulings got blended together, and the death penalty belongs only to פריעה and פרימה.

phrases.english: And if you heard something in the name of Shmuel,
this is what you heard:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב תַּחְלִיפָא בַּר אֲבִימִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Tachlifa bar Avimi said that Shmuel said:
A mourner who did not let his hair grow wild and did not tear his clothes
is liable to death,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי שְׁמִיעָא לְכוּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל, הָכִי שְׁמִיעַ לְכוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב פפא's correction by giving שמואל's real statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אבל who does not do פריעה and פרימה is liable to מיתה.

steps.title: The source: the verse told to אהרן's sons
steps.stepSummary: שמואל's ruling is learned from the פסוק that told אהרן's sons not to mourn 'so that you not die'. That means any other mourner who fails to mourn is liable to death.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'Do not let the hair of your heads grow wild, and do not tear your clothes, so that you do not die.' This implies that anyone else who did not let his hair grow wild and did not tear his clothes is liable to death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the פסוק behind שמואל's statement and makes a reverse inference from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אהרן's sons were told not to do פריעה and פרימה 'so that you not die'. For them, mourning would have brought death. The גמרא reasons that for every other אבל it is the opposite: not mourning is what makes him liable to death.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק)
This implies / from here we infer

phrases.english: as it is said: "Do not let the hair of your heads grow wild,
and do not tear your clothes,
so that you do not die, etc."

phrases.aramaic: הָא אַחֵר שֶׁלֹּא פֵּרַע וְשֶׁלֹּא פֵּירַם —
phrases.english: This implies that another who did not let his hair grow wild and did not tear his clothes
phrases.notes: 'Another' means any mourner besides אהרן's sons, who had been told not to mourn.

phrases.english: is liable to death.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: רָאשֵׁיכֶם אַל תִּפְרָעוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for שמואל's ruling in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's ruling that an אבל who skips פריעה and פרימה is liable to מיתה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 10:6, read in reverse: אהרן's sons were exempt from mourning 'so that you not die', so others who do not mourn are liable.

steps.title: אבל רבתי: relations are forbidden, and a frightening story
steps.stepSummary: רפרם בר פפא quotes אבל רבתי: an אבל may not have relations during his mourning days. It also tells of a man who did, and pigs dragged away his body.
steps.simpleTranslation: רפרם בר פפא said: It was taught in אבל רבתי: A mourner is forbidden to have marital relations during his days of mourning. There was an incident with one who had relations during his days of mourning, and pigs dragged away his corpse.
steps.whatsHappening: רפרם בר פפא brings a ברייתא from אבל רבתי. It matches רב פפא's correction that the rule is 'אסור'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the word 'אסור', not 'חייב מיתה', which supports רב פפא's version of the ruling. The story shows that breaking the rule was still punished, with a disgraceful end after death.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Great Mourning', a separate collection of mourning laws

steps.whatToRemember: Relations during אבילות are אסור, not a death-penalty offense (רבי יוחנן, supported by אבל רבתי). The 'חייב מיתה' ruling of שמואל is about failing to do פריעה and פרימה.

phrases.english: Rafram bar Pappa said,
it was taught in Evel Rabbati:
A mourner is forbidden to have marital relations
during his days of mourning,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַעֲשֶׂה בְּאֶחָד שֶׁשִּׁימֵּשׁ מִטָּתוֹ בִּימֵי אֶבְלוֹ,
phrases.english: and there was an incident with one who had relations during his days of mourning,
and pigs dragged away his corpse.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַפְרָם בַּר פָּפָּא, תָּנָא בְּאֵבֶל רַבָּתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב פפא's corrected ruling (אסור) from step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That relations during אבילות are forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in אבל רבתי, along with a story of punishment.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: An אבל is forbidden to have relations during his mourning days.

steps.title: שמואל's memory-letters for mourning on שבת
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the mourning practices of פח״ז must be stopped on שבת, while those of נת״ר are optional.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: פח״ז are required, נת״ר are optional. Uncovering the head, turning the tear to the back, and standing the bed upright are required. Wearing shoes, marital relations, and washing hands and feet in hot water in the evening are optional.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a list, with memory-letters, of what an אבל must do on שבת and what he may choose to do. The גמרא then spells out what each letter stands for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'required' group covers visible signs of mourning that an אבל must undo on שבת: covering his head, showing his torn garment, and keeping his bed turned over. The 'optional' group covers things he may resume or keep avoiding as he likes. The first letter of each practice forms the memory-words פח״ז and נת״ר.

keyTerms.meaning: Required: the אבל must do it on שבת
Optional: the אבל may choose whether to do it
Uncovering the head, taking off the mourner's head-wrap
Turning the torn part of the garment to the back so it is not seen
Standing the bed upright instead of leaving it turned over

steps.confusionAlert: 'Required' here does not mean a mourning practice is required. It means the אבל is required to STOP the mourning sign and act normally, in honor of שבת.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
P-Ch-Z are required,
phrases.notes: These are just memory letters. The next lines tell you what each letter stands for.

phrases.english: N-T-R are optional.
Uncovering the head,
turning the tear around to the back,
standing the bed upright: these are required.
Wearing shoes, marital relations,

phrases.aramaic: רְחִיצַת יָדַיִם וְרַגְלַיִם בְּחַמִּין עַרְבִית — רְשׁוּת.
phrases.english: washing hands and feet in hot water in the evening: these are optional.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: פַּחַ״ז חוֹבָה, נֶתֶ״ר רְשׁוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about mourning practices on שבת, after the earlier discussion of an אבל and marital relations.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שבת an אבל must uncover his head, turn his tear to the back, and set his bed upright. Shoes, marital relations, and hot-water washing are up to him.

steps.title: רב says uncovering the head is also optional
steps.stepSummary: רב disagrees about one item: he holds that uncovering the head is also optional.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב said: uncovering the head is also optional.
steps.whatsHappening: רב argues with שמואל about one item and moves uncovering the head into the optional group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, an אבל does not have to take off his head-wrap on שבת. That leaves only two required items. This disagreement sets up the next question about שמואל's reasoning.

phrases.english: And Rav said:
Uncovering the head is also optional.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב אָמַר: אַף פְּרִיעַת הָרֹאשׁ רְשׁוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with one item in שמואל's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Uncovering the head on שבת is optional for an אבל.

steps.title: Why are shoes optional but uncovering the head required?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל: if shoes are optional because not everyone wears them, the same should be true for uncovering the head.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to שמואל, what is different about wearing shoes that it is optional? Because not everyone wears shoes. Uncovering the head too: not everyone goes with his head uncovered!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why שמואל treats the two cases differently when they look the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that something is optional when skipping it does not clearly show mourning. Going barefoot is not a clear sign, because many people go without shoes anyway. But many people also keep their heads covered, so a covered head should not be a clear sign either. So uncovering the head should also be optional, like רב says.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Why treat this case differently?
They wear (literally, put on) their shoes

phrases.english: And according to Shmuel, what is different about
wearing shoes, that it is optional?
Because not everyone is used to
wearing their shoes.
Uncovering the head as well:
not everyone is used to
going with their heads uncovered!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל, מַאי שְׁנָא נְעִילַת הַסַּנְדָּל דִּרְשׁוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's split between shoes and the head-wrap, using the reasoning that fits רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that uncovering the head is required
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same reason that makes shoes optional (not everyone does it, so it is not a clear sign of mourning) should apply to a covered head too.

steps.title: שמואל requires a special, unusual head-wrap
steps.stepSummary: שמואל holds that a mourner's wrap must be like the wrap of the ישמעאלים. Nobody normally wraps that way, so it is a clear sign of mourning and must be removed on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל follows his own reasoning, since שמואל said: any tear not made at the time of the most intense grief is not a tear, and any wrapping that is not like the wrapping of the ישמעאלים is not a wrapping.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שמואל's ruling fits another statement of his about how a mourner must wrap his head.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, a proper mourner's wrap covers most of the face, the way the ישמעאלים wrap. People do not normally go around like that, so anyone who sees it knows he is mourning. Shoes are different, so they stay optional. The line about the tear is quoted only because it is part of the same statement of שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning from elsewhere
The time of the most intense grief, right at the death
Wrapping the head as a mourner
The way the ישמעאלים wrap: covering most of the face

steps.whatToRemember: According to שמואל, the head-wrap must be removed on שבת because his kind of wrap is unusual and clearly shows mourning, while going without shoes does not.

phrases.english: Shmuel follows his own reasoning,
for Shmuel said:
Any tear that is not made at the time of the most intense grief
is not a tear.
And any wrapping that is not
like the wrapping of the Ishmaelites
is not a wrapping.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמוּאֵל לְטַעְמֵיהּ, דְּאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by defining what a mourner's head-wrap is according to שמואל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the case differently: the wrap שמואל means is unusual, unlike ordinary head-covering.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A mourner's covered head looks like anyone else's covered head, so uncovering it should be optional.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל's mourner's wrap is the ישמעאלים style, which clearly shows mourning, so it must be removed on שבת.

steps.title: רב נחמן shows how far the wrap goes
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן demonstrates the ישמעאלים-style wrap, covering down to the sides of the beard.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן demonstrated: down to the sides of the beard.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן shows with his own head-covering what the ישמעאלים-style wrap looks like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wrap covers the head and comes down around the face as far as the sides of the beard. This makes clear how different it is from ordinary head-covering.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman demonstrated:
down to the sides of the beard.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַחְוֵי רַב נַחְמָן עַד גּוּבֵּי דְּדִיקְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows in practice what the ישמעאלים wrap from the previous step looks like.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The mourner's wrap covers the face down to the sides of the beard.

steps.title: Shoes show he is not mourning
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the head must be uncovered on שבת only when the mourner is barefoot. If he wears shoes, the shoes already show he is not mourning publicly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב said in the name of רבי יוחנן: This rule applies only when the mourner has no shoes on. If he has shoes on, his shoes show that he is not mourning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds a limit to the rule that a mourner must uncover his head on שבת. The rule applies only when he is also barefoot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Going barefoot together with a wrapped head would make the mourning very obvious on שבת. But if he is wearing shoes, everyone can already see he is not keeping mourning practices. So the wrapped head alone is not a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only in the case of; a phrase that limits a rule
They prove about him; they make his situation clear

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, wearing shoes on שבת already shows that the mourner is not mourning, so the head does not also need to be uncovered.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
They taught this only
phrases.notes: He means the rule that a mourner must uncover his wrapped head on שבת.

phrases.english: when he has no shoes on his feet,
but if he has shoes on his feet —
his shoes prove about him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the head-uncovering rule discussed in steps 8-12
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Uncovering the head on שבת is required only when the mourner is barefoot. With shoes on, the shoes show he is not mourning.

steps.title: Tearing for a sage after hearing the news
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes שמואל's rule that tearing counts only at the moment of intense grief. It challenges the rule from שמואל tearing for רב, and רבי יוחנן tearing for רבי חנינא, when they only heard the news later.
steps.simpleTranslation: Any tearing that is not done at the time of intense grief is not a real tearing. But when they told שמואל that רב had died, he tore twelve garments and said, 'The man I feared is gone.' And when they told רבי יוחנן that רבי חנינא had died, he tore thirteen wool robes and said, 'The man I feared is gone.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to שמואל's rule about קריעה. It challenges the rule with two stories of great אמוראים who tore their garments when they heard about a death later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule says tearing counts only in the first moment of strong grief. In both stories, the news came after that moment had passed. Even so, these great sages tore, and they tore many garments.

keyTerms.meaning: A tear in a garment made for mourning
The time of intense, 'hot' grief, right at the death
His soul rested; he passed away
I was afraid of, I stood in awe of

phrases.english: Any tearing that is not at the time of intense grief
is not a tearing —
But they said to Shmuel:
Rav has passed away,
and he tore twelve garments over him.
He said: The man has gone
whom I was in fear of.
They said to Rabbi Yochanan:
Rabbi Chanina has passed away.
He tore thirteen wool robes over him.
He said: The man has gone
whom I was in fear of!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ לִשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the first half of the same statement of שמואל quoted in step 11 (about קריעה בשעת חימום) and opens a new challenge
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that קריעה not done בשעת חימום does not count
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל himself, and also רבי יוחנן, tore garments after hearing the news later, when the moment of intense grief had already passed.

steps.title: Sages are always like the moment of grief
steps.stepSummary: Torah scholars are different. Their teachings are quoted all the time, so the grief keeps coming back, and any time counts as the moment of intense grief.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sages are different. Since their teachings are mentioned all the time, every time is like the moment of intense grief.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It says the rule stays the same, but with a תלמיד חכם the time of intense grief never really ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every time someone quotes the sage's teaching, people remember the loss and the pain comes back. So hearing the news later still counts as שעת חימום. This is a special outcome inside שמואל's rule; it does not cancel the rule.

phrases.english: The Sages are different,
since all the time
their teachings are mentioned —
it is like the time of intense grief.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes a special case: a תלמיד חכם
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Tearing late for a sage seemed to go against the rule of שעת חימום.
steps.terutzMaskana: For a sage, the grief keeps coming back whenever his teachings are quoted, so it is always considered שעת חימום.

steps.title: A mourner tears new garments all seven days
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reported by רב עמרם says a mourner who changes clothes during the seven days tears the new garment too. That seems to show tearing counts even after the moment of intense grief.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבין בר אדא said to רבא: Your student רב עמרם said that a ברייתא teaches: A mourner keeps his tear in front of him all seven days. If he changes clothes, he changes and tears the new one. On שבת, he turns the tear to his back. If he changes clothes, he changes and does not tear.
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge to שמואל's rule comes from a ברייתא. It teaches that during the week of mourning, a mourner must tear a fresh garment whenever he changes clothes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If tearing counts only at the first moment of grief, there should be no reason to tear a new garment days later. Yet the ברייתא requires it for all seven days, except on שבת. That seems to go against שמואל.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 14. There the late tearing was for a sage. Here the ברייתא is about any mourner tearing new clothes during the whole week.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִין בַּר אַדָּא לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Ravin bar Adda said to Rava:
Your student Rav Amram said,
it is taught: A mourner,
all seven days, keeps his tear in front of him,
and if he comes to change —
he changes and tears.
On Shabbat, he keeps his tear behind him,
and if he comes to change —
he changes and does not tear!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִין בַּר אַדָּא לְרָבָא: אָמַר תַּלְמִידְךָ רַב עַמְרָם, תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second challenge to שמואל's rule after the first was answered
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that קריעה must be בשעת חימום
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא requires a mourner to tear new garments throughout the seven days, long after the first moment of grief, and not only for a sage.

steps.title: The new-garment rule applies only to a parent
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא about tearing a new garment during the seven days speaks only about mourning for a father or mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: When that ברייתא was taught, it was about the honor of one's father and mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 16. The ברייתא's rule of tearing each new garment applies only when mourning a parent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's rule still holds: normally, tearing counts only at the moment of intense grief. A parent is a special exception. Out of כבוד אב ואם, the child should not wear a whole garment during the seven days, so he tears each new one.

keyTerms.meaning: The honor due to one's father and mother
When that teaching was taught (it was about...)

steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not cancel שמואל's rule. It only makes mourning for a parent an exception to it.

phrases.english: When that one was taught,
phrases.notes: "That one" is the ברייתא רב עמרם reported, about tearing the new garment.

phrases.english: it was about the honor of his father and mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי תַּנְיָא הָהִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 16 by limiting the ברייתא to mourning for parents.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the ברייתא is a special case for parents.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to show that tearing counts after the moment of intense grief for any relative.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only for a parent must the new garment be torn, because of כבוד אב ואם. שמואל's general rule stands.

steps.title: May the extra tears for a parent be mended?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the additional tears made on new garments for a parent may later be properly sewn up.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those tears: may they be properly mended, or may they not be properly mended?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about the extra tears from step 17. Is the mourner allowed to sew them back properly later?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tear made for a parent at the moment of grief may never be properly mended. The question is whether the later tears, made only for the parent's honor, have the same strict status.

keyTerms.meaning: Tears made in clothing for mourning

phrases.english: Those tears, may they be mended,
phrases.notes: "Those tears" are the extra ones made on new garments during the seven days for a parent.

phrases.english: or may they not be mended?

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹתָן קְרָעִין מִתְאַחִין, אוֹ אֵין מִתְאַחִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the new rule from step 17 and asks about its details.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do the extra tears for a parent share the no-mending rule of the original tear?

steps.title: A dispute between רב אושעיא's father and בר קפרא
steps.stepSummary: Two אמוראים disagree. One says the tears may not be mended, and the other says they may.
steps.simpleTranslation: The father of רב אושעיא and בר קפרא disagree about this. One said: they may not be mended. The other said: they may be mended.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by reporting a מחלוקת. It does not yet say who held which opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The side that says they may not be mended treats the later tears like the original tear for a parent. The side that says they may be mended sees them as a lesser tear, made only for honor.

keyTerms.meaning: One said... and one said (without telling us who said which)

phrases.english: They disagree about it:
the father of Rav Oshaya and bar Kappara.
One said: they may not be mended,
and one said: they may be mended.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ אֲבוּהּ דְּרַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא וּבַר קַפָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18 with an unattributed מחלוקת.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is a מחלוקת: one view forbids mending, and the other allows it.

steps.title: An attempt to show רב אושעיא's father forbade mending
steps.stepSummary: Since רב אושעיא himself ruled that the tears may not be mended, the גמרא suggests he learned this from his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: Conclude that it was רב אושעיא's father who said they may not be mended. For רב אושעיא said: they may not be mended. From whom did he hear it? Was it not from his father?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to figure out who said which opinion. It uses a ruling that רב אושעיא gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic is that a son usually learns from his father. So רב אושעיא's ruling would show his father's position. That would make בר קפרא the one who allowed mending.

keyTerms.meaning: From whom did he hear it?

phrases.english: Conclude that it was Rav Oshaya's father
who said they may not be mended.
For Rav Oshaya said: they may not be mended,
from whom did he hear it?
Was it not from his father?

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּסְתַּיֵּים דַּאֲבוּהּ דְּרַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא דְּאָמַר אֵין מִתְאַחִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to identify who held each side of the מחלוקת in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: That רב אושעיא's father held the tears may not be mended
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב אושעיא's own ruling, presumably learned from his father

steps.title: He may have learned it from his teacher instead
steps.stepSummary: The proof fails. רב אושעיא could have heard the ruling from בר קפרא, who was his teacher.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, he heard it from בר קפרא, his teacher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 20. רב אושעיא had another possible source for his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בר קפרא was רב אושעיא's רבי. A student can learn from his teacher just as easily as from his father. So the ruling does not show who said what, and the question is left open.
steps.whatToRemember: The extra tears for a parent are a מחלוקת regarding mending. We cannot tell for sure which of the two אמוראים held which view.

phrases.english: No, from bar Kappara, his teacher,
he heard it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, מִבַּר קַפָּרָא רַבֵּיהּ שְׁמִיעַ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. The מחלוקת itself is unchanged.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed רב אושעיא's only possible source was his father. He could have learned it from his teacher, בר קפרא.

steps.title: A mourner may wear a torn robe inside his house
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that on שבת a mourner may walk around his house in his torn robe.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: a mourner may walk around in a robe inside his house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: mourning practices on שבת done in private. רבא allows the torn robe at home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת there is no public mourning, so a mourner may not show his torn garment outside. Inside his own house no one sees it, so it does not count as public mourning.

keyTerms.meaning: A robe (here, his torn mourning garment)

phrases.english: Rava said:
A mourner may walk around in a robe
phrases.notes: This means his torn robe, worn on שבת.

phrases.english: inside his house.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אָבֵל מְטַיֵּיל בְּאוּנְקְלִי בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling about mourning on שבת. It returns to the theme of steps 1-2 (אין אבילות בשבת) and steps 8-13 (which mourning signs are dropped on שבת), now about private conduct at home.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mourner may wear his torn robe in private, inside his home, on שבת.

steps.title: אביי questions רב יוסף mourning at home on שבת
steps.stepSummary: אביי saw רב יוסף with a mourner's head-covering in his house on שבת. He asked: isn't there no mourning on שבת?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי found רב יוסף with a scarf spread over his head, walking back and forth in his house. He said to him: Doesn't the master hold that there is no mourning on שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: A story is told, and inside it אביי challenges רב יוסף. רב יוסף's behavior seems to go against the rule that there is no mourning on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Covering the head was a sign of mourning (see steps 12-13). Since שבת has no mourning, אביי assumes רב יוסף should not be practicing any sign of mourning, even at home.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no mourning on שבת

phrases.english: Abaye found Rav Yosef
with a scarf spread over his head,
walking back and forth in his house.
He said to him:
Doesn't the master hold
that there is no mourning on Shabbat?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו סָבַר לַהּ מָר אֵין אֲבֵילוּת בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that illustrates and tests the private-mourning idea of step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's practice of covering his head at home on שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is no mourning on שבת, so any sign of mourning, even at home, should be forbidden.

steps.title: Private mourning practices do apply on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers by quoting רבי יוחנן: mourning practices done in private are kept even on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רבי יוחנן said: things done in private apply.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers אביי's question. He explains that the rule of no mourning on שבת covers only public mourning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on mourning on שבת is about public display. Private practices, done where no one sees, stay in force. This also gives the reason behind רבא's ruling in step 22.
steps.whatToRemember: On שבת, public mourning is forbidden. Private mourning practices, like those done inside one's house, still apply.
steps.confusionAlert: "אֵין אֲבֵילוּת בְּשַׁבָּת" does not mean mourning stops completely on שבת. It means no mourning in public.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic halachic principle for how a mourner behaves on שבת: hidden practices continue, and visible ones stop.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Matters that are in private, he observes.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: דְּבָרִים שֶׁבְּצִינְעָא נוֹהֵג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the scope of a rule: no mourning on שבת applies only to public mourning.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי thought all mourning stops on שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only public mourning is suspended. Private practices continue.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A mourner keeps his private mourning practices on שבת.

steps.title: The halacha follows רבן גמליאל on holidays and mourning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's dispute about which holidays act like festivals for mourning. רב גידל בר מנשיא, quoting שמואל, rules like רבן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי אליעזר says that since the בית המקדש was destroyed, עצרת is like שבת, and so on. רב גידל בר מנשיא said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה follows רבן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to a line of the משנה about holidays and mourning. It gives a final ruling: we follow רבן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי אליעזר says that since the חורבן, עצרת counts only like שבת for mourning, not like a full festival. רבן גמליאל makes a different claim: ראש השנה and יום כיפור count like festivals. שמואל rules like רבן גמליאל, so those days have a festival's power over mourning.

keyTerms.meaning: The name the משנה uses for שבועות
"Etc." It means the rest of the quoted text continues
The final law follows this opinion

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical ruling on how ראש השנה and יום כיפור affect a mourner: like a festival, following רבן גמליאל.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
Since the Temple was destroyed,
Shavuot is like Shabbat, etc.
phrases.notes: The "etc." points to the rest of the משנה, where רבן גמליאל says ראש השנה and יום כיפור are like festivals.

phrases.english: Rav Giddel bar Menashya said
Shmuel said:
The halacha follows Rabban Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל בַּר מְנַשְּׁיָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. The גמרא moves from wearing mourning clothes on שבת to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבן גמליאל: ראש השנה and יום כיפור count like festivals for mourning.

steps.title: Another version places the ruling on the baby-burial ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: Some teach that רב גידל בר מנשיא's ruling was said about a different source. That source is a ברייתא about carrying and burying a baby who died within thirty days of birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach this ruling of רב גידל בר מנשיא as said about the following: for the first thirty days, a baby who dies is carried out in a person's arms. He is buried by one woman and two men, but not by one man and two women.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of where רב גידל בר מנשיא's ruling belongs. It quotes the ברייתא it was attached to, which sets up the ruling being placed on this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, רב גידל's ruling was not about holidays at all. It was about the laws of burying a baby. The ברייתא says a baby this young is carried in someone's arms, not in a coffin, and a small group may bury him. Two men may go with one woman, but one man may not go with two women.

keyTerms.meaning: And some teach it this way. This introduces a second version
On this, meaning attached to the following source
In the bosom, carried in a person's arms

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think there are two different rulings here. It is one statement of רב גידל בר מנשיא, and the two versions only disagree about which source it was said on.

phrases.english: And some teach

phrases.aramaic: לְהָא דְּרַב גִּידֵּל בַּר מְנַשְּׁיָא אַהָא:
phrases.english: this ruling of Rav Giddel bar Menashya as referring to the following:
Within the first thirty days,
phrases.notes: He means the first thirty days after the baby is born.

phrases.english: an infant is taken out in one's bosom,
phrases.notes: He is carried to the grave in someone's arms, not in a coffin.

phrases.english: and he is buried by one woman and two men.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא בְּאִישׁ אֶחָד וּשְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים.
phrases.english: But not by one man and two women.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּמַתְנֵי לְהָא דְּרַב גִּידֵּל בַּר מְנַשְּׁיָא אַהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of where the ruling in step 25 was said, moving it from the משנה about holidays to a ברייתא about burying a baby.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A baby who dies within thirty days of birth is carried in the arms and may be buried by one woman and two men, but not by one man and two women. רב גידל's ruling is attached to this source.
